proposal_title: JSON Schema Root Packaging & Fragment Entrypoint Documentation
domain_specific_rationale: As the Developer Experience Architect with mandatory signoff authority, schema usability, CLI tooling ergonomics, and deterministic automated validation are fundamental responsibilities. Packaging domain-entities.schema.json as a definitions bundle without documenting root validation semantics caused immediate developer and agent confusion (TECH-017 / M05), as standard validator tools (ajv validate, jsonschema, pydantic) fail when instances of specific aggregates (Project, ShotVersion, GenerationJob) are validated directly against the un-fragmented schema root. CP-022 resolves this DX barrier by formally specifying fragment entrypoint syntax (#/$defs/Project, #/$defs/ShotVersion, #/$defs/Take, etc.) and root packaging behavior in 02_contracts/CONTRACTS_OVERVIEW.md, while documenting exact CLI, Node.js, and Python code snippets for multi-schema fragment resolution. This ensures zero friction for developers writing integration test fixtures and autonomous agents building domain validation layers.
capability_impact: Strengthens CAP-02 (Canonical State & Data Consistency) and CAP-16 (Hermetic Simulation & Testing) by providing standardized, frictionless schema validation mechanics across all 15 repositories and client SDKs.
residual_risk: Certain older schema validator libraries may struggle with nested dynamic $ref fragment resolution across bundled JSON schemas. Mitigated by providing pre-bundled dereferenced schema exports in avf-contracts package distribution and documenting standard Ajv/Pydantic configuration templates.
